tasks.title: [M1-07] Freeze the four measurement definitions and shared benchmark inputs
acceptance: For prediction quality, training cost, inference cost, and disk or memory size, write metric / data / operationalization.
Agree exact dataset hashes, held-out pairs, relevance threshold, candidate catalog, K=20, seen-item rules and eligible users.
Use identical hardware and documented thread settings; separate warm/cold inference and disclose excluded costs.
Agree per-user split limitation or a better shared split; do not compare incompatible M0 scores.

tasks.title: [M1-08] Run all four models and produce the comparison table
acceptance: Each member runs their model under the agreed protocol; Nathan consolidates results.
Populate all four required qualities for all four models with units and source commit links.
Save measurement code, raw outputs, repeat counts and environment details.
Do not mark missing results as zero; record and resolve failures.

tasks.title: [M1-09] Choose the production model and record the trade-offs
acceptance: Review quality, speed, training cost and size jointly with all members.
Record selected model and reason; discuss at least one rejected alternative.
Identify any adaptations and freeze a model artifact/version for deployment.
Update responsibilities if the chosen model changes the service or cold-start plan.

tasks.title: [M1-10] Implement the exact recommendation HTTP contract
acceptance: Implement GET /recommend/<userid> exposed on VM port 8082.
Return one line of up to 20 valid unique movie IDs, comma-separated and ordered best first; no JSON, titles or scores.
Load model at startup, avoid retraining or LLM generation inside the request, and handle missing users promptly.
Verify known, new and invalid-user behavior and record end-to-end latency; course timeout is 600 ms.

tasks.title: [M1-11] Automate cold start for new live users
acceptance: Consume account_created events and fetch the user’s likes/dislikes from the live API.
Generate LLM interpretations automatically in a background worker and persist versioned profiles.
Allow inference for IDs absent from the offline fitted users list; a new profile must not require full retraining.
Use a fast pending-profile fallback, retries and deduplication; demonstrate a new user receiving personalized recommendations after profile completion.
Measure time to profile readiness and LLM resource/API cost separately; static profiles for the original 50 users alone are insufficient.

tasks.title: [M1-12] Verify VM, Kafka and metadata API access
acceptance: Confirm all teammates can SSH to the assigned VM and locate course-provided Kafka/API settings.
Verify disk, memory, Docker/Compose availability and VM reachability on the required service port.
Keep credentials out of Git; record reproducible environment setup and .env.example variable names only.
Resolve infrastructure blockers with course staff early.
tasks.rubric: Prerequisite for live service and deployment

tasks.title: [M1-13] Containerize service and cold-start worker with Docker Compose
acceptance: Commit Dockerfile(s), compose.yaml, dependency versions and startup commands.
Serve on 0.0.0.0 inside the container with host port 8082 exposed; load a versioned model at startup.
Integrate cold-start worker and durable profile storage in Compose, with environment-based configuration.
Demonstrate docker compose up -d --build from documented prerequisites; ensure a restart preserves profiles.

tasks.title: [M1-14] Deploy to the team VM and verify reproduction
acceptance: Deploy a specific committed version over SSH using repository-owned commands.
Record deployed commit/model version and smoke-test the external VM URL.
Have a second teammate reproduce startup using the runbook; put lasting fixes in Git.
Aim for Saturday deployment to leave a full day for course traffic and fixes; keep rollback instructions.

tasks.title: [M1-15] Verify real course requests and Kafka success records
acceptance: Locate recommendation-request records for this team's server in movielog.
Verify status 200, parsed ordered movie IDs and response time <=600 ms.
Record the exact timestamp window and evidence location; distinguish course traffic from self-generated tests.
Investigate parsing, network or timeout failures while there is time to fix them.

tasks.title: [M1-16] Track the 24-hour success and personalization targets
acceptance: Compute successful requests and total requests over the applicable 24-hour grading window.
Demonstrate >=2,000 successful course requests and personalized successful requests / ALL requests >=10%.
Use route-level service logs plus course responses to identify real personalization; different lists alone do not prove personalization.
Check live-user coverage; offline 1,000-user training coverage may be too small. Track unknown-user and pending-profile rates.
Keep monitoring through the chosen before/after-submission window; do not stop after 2,000 successes.

tasks.title: [M1-17] Write model comparison and prediction-service report sections
acceptance: Create m1_report.md at the team repository root.
Comparison: <=1 page of text plus table, four three-step metrics, all four model results and M0 links, selection argument, measurement code links.
Service: <=1 page explaining ranking, changes to selected model, and how/when live cold start runs; link training and inference implementation.
State limitations honestly and use observed results only.

tasks.title: [M1-18] Document deployment architecture and runbook
acceptance: Write <=0.5-page containerization/deployment section with links to Dockerfiles, Compose and runbook.
Include one compact architecture view with a named question, separating request logic, model component and cold-start path.
Explain a concrete trade-off: e.g. background profile generation protects latency but new users wait for personalization.
State deployment and persistence behavior; do not depict components that were not implemented.

tasks.title: [M1-19] Review all rubric evidence and cross-teach the solution

Check all report links, four-model table, who/what/due-date notes, board and issue links.
Verify report descriptions match running code and all required evidence exists.
Check course staff repository access and confirm each task has an actual assignee and due date.
